description: FILM SCORING and orchestral arrangement: a WHOLE ARRANGEMENT in one call (a film cue, a string quartet, a big-band chart): every part played by its doseedo instrument, one stem per part from bar 1 at your tempo, plus a summed mix. Input ONE of: parts[] ({name, instrument, timbre_preset?, lora_id?, players?, notes[]} — doseedo_instruments calls), midi_url (multi-track SMF), or musicxml_url (dynamics, hairpins, staccato/accents, pizz./arco, con sord. are performed; concert pitch). A file's parts are matched by name, then GM program; name any part with instruments {"<part name or index>": {instrument, timbre_preset?, players?}}. A chord on a one-line instrument is split into voices (one stem each). ★ SECTIONS: an instrument is ONE player; give a part players: N (2–8) and its line is played by N different players (each its own recording and performance), summed into ONE section stem — that is how you write an orchestra: violins I / violins II / violas / cellos / basses as five parts with players 6 / 6 / 4 / 4 / 3, horns 2–4 in unison, a woodwind or brass line doubled; leave players out for a solo. The WHOLE orchestra in one call: ≤ 32 lines (≤ 96 players), plain, sampled and World / LoRA instruments together (played in groups, ~1 min each). No synth / electronic parts (doseedo_render_midi), ≤ 600 s. Timing: bpm and/or tempo_map ([{beat, bpm}]; doseedo_tempo_map lands film hits on downbeats). Result: parts[{name, instrument, url, fit, timbre, lora, players}] — fit.verdict / coverage = did it PLAY its notes (a failed part is re-rolled once), lora.applied = its adapter played — plus mix_url. Next: doseedo_mix {from_job}, then doseedo_session_from_stems {from_job, mix_job}. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~1–4 min). Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

bpm.description: Tempo of the parts (10–400). Required with parts[] unless tempo_map is given; overrides a file's own tempo.

duration_seconds.description: Render length (default: the last note + 2 s; ≤ 600).

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

instruments.description: Name the instrument for any part: {"Violin I": {"instrument": "violin", "players": 6}, "2": {"instrument": "acoustic_guitar", "timbre_preset": "koto:preset1"}} — key = the part name or its 0-based index; players makes a MIDI / MusicXML part a section. Wins over the name/program match.

midi_url.description: Alternative to parts: a multi-track Standard MIDI File (≤ 2 MiB) — a doseedo result link or a public https URL. Channel 10 = drums.

mix.description: Also bounce a summed mix of the stems (default true).

musicxml_url.description: Alternative to parts: a MusicXML score (.musicxml / .xml / .mxl, ≤ 8 MiB) exported from Dorico, Sibelius, Finale, MuseScore, or written by you.

parts.description: The parts you wrote: [{name?, instrument, timbre_preset?, lora_id?, players?, notes:[{pitch, start_beats, duration_beats, velocity?}]}] — beats from bar 1, concert pitch. instrument/timbre_preset = a doseedo_instruments call. players = how many play the line: 1 (default) a soloist, 2–8 a SECTION (e.g. Violins I players 6).

dynamics_curve.description: What colours this part's TONE over time: auto (default) = its note velocities when they vary — soft notes darker, loud notes brighter, on every instrument but drums; off = one colour throughout; cc11/cc1 = that MIDI CC lane (a midi_url part). Receipt: parts[].dynamics.

players.description: How many players play this line: 1 (default) = a soloist; 2–8 = a SECTION — the line played by that many different players (each its own recording and performance), summed into ONE section stem. A string section = violins I, violins II, violas, cellos, basses with players 4–8 each. Each player renders (and costs) like a part.

tune.description: false = this part exactly as rendered (no light intonation pass; default true).

score_url.description: Alternative to parts: a score file URL — MIDI or MusicXML, told apart by its content.

seed.description: Random seed (reuse to re-render close to the same performance).

tempo_map.description: Tempo changes [{beat, bpm}] (first point at beat 0). Overrides a file's own tempo.

tune.description: Light intonation on every winds / brass / strings part (default true): held, clearly pitched notes the model rendered 15–85 cents off are moved toward their written pitch, to a small natural residual — attacks, vibrato and fast notes as played. Receipt: parts[].tune. false = every part as rendered (or parts[].tune false for one).

name: doseedo_render_score
title: Render a whole score
